author: pereanub
title: ARM64 cross-compilation build fails with cc1plus: not a PCH file (invalid-pch) in openvino_reference
signature: cc1plus error cmake_pch hxx gch not a pch file werror invalid pch|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: CMake configure, build and install - OpenVINO JS API step fails: cc1plus reports cmake_pch.hxx.gch is not a valid PCH file, turned into a hard error by -Werror=invalid-pch

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: Downstream status-aggregation job fails because the upstream Build job failed (exit 1 by design)

key_errors: cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]
root_cause: The failure occurs during the separate 'CMake configure, build and install - OpenVINO JS API' re-configure/rebuild step, which re-runs cmake with -UTBB* -DCPACK_GENERATOR=NPM -DENABLE_SYSTEM_TBB=OFF -DENABLE_WHEEL=OFF against the SAME build directory already populated by the earlier Release build (with a different config: -DENABLE_WHEEL=ON, -DENABLE_PYTHON=ON, etc.). The precompiled header (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) that was generated for openvino_reference in the first build pass is stale/incompatible once compiler flags change for the JS API reconfiguration, so GCC's cc1plus rejects it as 'not a PCH file'. Because CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON, this is escalated from a (recoverable) PCH cache-staleness warning into a hard build failure (-Werror=invalid-pch). This is the same signature recorded 14 times previously across many unrelated PRs over the last two weeks, confirming it is an infrastructure/build-cache issue in the ARM64 cross-compile pipeline rather than anything in this PR's NPU-focused changes (device_helpers.cpp/hpp, plugin_property_manager.cpp, functional/unit tests) — none of which touch PCH, CMake, or core/reference code.
reproduction_steps: N/A (requires the shared ARM64 cross-compile build directory/sccache state from the Build job; not reliably reproducible locally without the same stale cmake_pch.hxx.gch artifact). Locally: configure Release build with PCH enabled, build src/core/reference, then re-run cmake with a different config (e.g. toggling ENABLE_WHEEL/ENABLE_PYTHON) against the same build dir without clearing the PCH, and rebuild the reference target.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed jobs (this failure clears on retry since it is a stale-PCH/build-cache artifact, not a code defect)

Long-term: force a clean/rebuild of the PCH artifact (or disable PCH, or isolate it per cmake configuration) when the JS API re-configure step changes compiler-affecting options against the same build directory
Consider using a separate build directory for the JS API NPM reconfigure step instead of reusing BUILD_DIR, to avoid cross-configuration PCH contamination

Alternatively, downgrade invalid-pch handling to a warning instead of an error for this specific re-configure+rebuild path, or explicitly `rm -f $BUILD_DIR/.../cmake_pch.hxx.gch` before the JS API cmake invocation
prevention_strategies: Avoid reusing a single CMake build directory across build configurations that change compiler-relevant flags (TBB/wheel/python toggles) when precompiled headers are enabled; either use distinct build dirs per configuration or invalidate/rebuild the PCH when the configuration changes. Track this known recurring infra issue and prioritize a permanent fix given its high occurrence count (15 times in two weeks).
historical_context: This exact signature has been recorded 14 times before this run (now 15), affecting unrelated PRs (#38407, #38601, #38559, #37717, #38261, #37908, #38604, #38607, #38611, #38030, and others) across the last two weeks, all on the ARM64 cross-compilation ('ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation') pipeline. It consistently clears on job rerun, confirming it is a known transient infrastructure defect in that pipeline rather than a code-level regression.
